ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows quadrilateral TWYZ, with vertices forming a trapezoid in the order T-W-Y-Z; TW is the upper horizontal base, and ZY is the lower horizontal base. T is at the upper left, W is at the upper right, Z is at the lower left, and Y is at the lower right. In the figure, T and W have the same double-arc angle markings, indicating ∠T ≅ ∠W; Z and Y have the same single-arc angle markings, indicating ∠Z ≅ ∠Y. Reasoning: Because TWYZ is a trapezoid and TW ∥ ZY, the consecutive interior angles ∠T and ∠Z on the same leg TZ are supplementary, that is, ∠T + ∠Z = 180°. The problem gives m∠T = 20x and m∠Z = 30x, so 20x + 30x = 180, obtaining 50x = 180, x = 3.6. Thus m∠T = 20x = 20(3.6) = 72°. Also because ∠T ≅ ∠W, m∠W = 72°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: TWYZ is drawn as a trapezoid with TW as the top base and ZY as the bottom base, so the vertices go around the quadrilateral T-W-Y-Z. The top base angles at T and W are marked congruent, and the bottom base angles at Z and Y are marked congruent. From the text, use m∠Z = 30x and m∠T = 20x, with ∠T congruent to ∠W. Since TWYZ is a trapezoid, consecutive interior angles along a leg are supplementary; along leg TZ, ∠T + ∠Z = 180°. Set 20x + 30x = 180, so 50x = 180 and x = 3.6. Then m∠T = 20x = 72°. Because ∠T ≅ ∠W, m∠W = 72°.
